subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw adopt an opt-in core TUI text-presentation mode, and if so what exact replacement vocabulary and pi-tui boundary should it guarantee?
rationale: The report is well-supported, but the permanent config shape and whether dependency-owned selection indicators belong in the contract are user-facing compatibility decisions rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded ASCII TUI mode
options.body: Add one documented opt-in TUI presentation setting with a stable ASCII vocabulary, covering OpenClaw-owned symbols and any supported pi-tui theme seam.

options.title: Limit the first scope to OpenClaw-owned output
options.body: Replace tool, status, and theme glyphs now while documenting dependency-owned selector glyphs as separate upstream work.

options.title: Defer pending accessibility design input
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers and screen-reader users agree on vocabulary and the desired scope for framework-rendered selectors.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded ASCII TUI mode
recommendation.body: Add one documented opt-in TUI presentation setting with a stable ASCII vocabulary, covering OpenClaw-owned symbols and any supported pi-tui theme seam.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history most strongly connects this person to the original TUI and central tool-display/config paths involved in the contract choice.
